newsitem.title: GERMANY: German tax reform has no chance in Bundesrat - SPD.
newsitem.headline: German tax reform has no chance in Bundesrat - SPD.

text.p: Finance Minister Theo Waigel's tax reform does not stand a chance of passage in the upper house of parliament, the Bundesrat, which is dominated by the opposition Social Democrats (SPD), SPD leader Oskar Lafontaine said on Friday.
The tax reform, which includes 30 billion marks in tax cuts and a broadening of the tax base, was passed by the lower house on Thursday, and is due to go the upper house on July 4.
"All state premiers reject this bill," Lafontaine said in a radio interview. The upper chamber is made up of the state premiers and other state representatives.
Failure to pass the upper house would consign the bill to parliament's mediation procedure, but Lafontaine said he also sees little chance of success there.
"The problem of financing the tax cuts is too great, and there is no basis for negotiation," he said.
The SPD remains opposed to the government's plans to diminish tax breaks for commuters and those who work unsociable hours. There is also a need to coordinate with pension reform, Lafontaine said.
"It makes no sense to tax pensions and life insurance payouts, and then tell people they should be more responsible for their own financial security in their old age."

In response to coalition criticism that the SPD is blocking tax reform, Lafontaine said this should not divert from the fact that the coalition itself is divided on the issue. The coalition is no longer capable of negotiating, but does not want to give up power, he said.
"That is why little will move in German politics," he said.
